This site collects the reproducible analyses behind the IHC method study —
spatial single-cell IHC, bulk RNA-seq, cell-type deconvolution, clinical data,
and the image-registration / segmentation benchmarks that validate the pipeline.

The single-cell inputs come from the sibling repos: cells are segmented and
quantified by **mirage** (`../mirage`) and gated
independently in QuPath by **FlowPath** (`../qupath-extension-flowpath`); the
benchmark tables come from mirage's `benchmarks/` sweep. `code/cell_tables.R`
reconciles the export schemas and the two phenotype vocabularies those tools
produce, so every analysis here reads one vocabulary — see `code/README.md`.

## How the site is organised

Four parts, in the order the study is read. Each part is one claim, and the
navbar has one entry per part.

| part | claim | pages |
|---|---|---|
| **1 · Clinical** | cells land in the right region, and FlowPath's phenotypes agree with the pathologist | `clinical_massimo1` / `_massimo2` / `_massimo1_inverted`, `clinical_membership_qc` |
| **2 · Molecular** | bulk RNA, deconvolution and the invasive margin agree with the slide, and with the clinical hot/cold call | `molecular_massimo1` / `_massimo2` / `_massimo1_inverted` |
| **3 · Registration** | the study slides were registered well enough to analyse, under a configuration chosen on real tissue | `registration_run_qc`, `registration_arms` |
| **4 · Benchmarks** | the pipeline's cost and accuracy scale as claimed, measured on synthetic images | `benchmark_registration`, `benchmark_pipeline` |

The filename prefix is the part: anything `clinical_*` belongs to part 1,
`registration_*` to part 3, `benchmark_*` to part 4. Two pages sit outside the
four — `paper_figures` (the manuscript assembly sheet) and `marker_qc` (internal
gating QC that everything else assumes has passed).

Every page defines `SLUG` equal to its own filename and calls
`export_pdf_figures(SLUG)` last, so a page's vector figures always land in
`output/figures/<page name>/`.

## Part 1 — Clinical data and neoplastic concordance

Phenotypes come from **FlowPath's** QuPath gate tree; membership from the
pathologist's own polygons, region by region.

- Clinical concordance, **one page per phenotyping arm** —
  [Massimo1](clinical_massimo1.html) · [Massimo2](clinical_massimo2.html) ·
  [Massimo1 inverted](clinical_massimo1_inverted.html). Same analysis, three arms. A
  cell is inside when its centroid falls in **that region's own** polygon (sf
  point-in-polygon), because the all-slide export pairs a cell csv with a geojson
  region by region. A patient with no annotation directory is entirely inside — the
  layout's own convention, marked `whole_slide` rather than guessed. Includes the
  concordance against the pathologist's neoplastic-cellularity score.
- [Annotation membership QC](clinical_membership_qc.html) _(in progress)_ —
  sf point-in-polygon membership vs. the `Out_of_annotation` flag, compared per cell.
  This is the check the page above depends on: if membership itself is wrong, nothing
  downstream of it means anything.

## Part 2 — Bulk RNA, deconvolution and the hot/cold axis

- Bulk RNA, deconvolution and the hot/cold axis, **one page per arm** —
  [Massimo1](molecular_massimo1.html) · [Massimo2](molecular_massimo2.html) ·
  [Massimo1 inverted](molecular_massimo1_inverted.html) —
  three parts, one question: does a bulk readout agree with the slide, and does that
  agreement depend on whether the tumour is immunologically hot or cold?
  Part 1 is per-marker bulk expression vs the IHC positive-cell fraction; part 2 is
  `immunedeconv` cell-type scores vs the IHC lineage fractions; part 3 is the
  invasive-margin band (CD45+ fraction and density) against the clinical `HOT score`
  and immuno-phenotype. Points in parts 1 and 2 are coloured by that same clinical
  call, so a readout that only tracks IHC in hot tumours is visible as a colour split
  rather than hidden inside a middling correlation.

## Part 3 — Registration accuracy on the study run

These two read the **real slides**. They answer different questions and are not
interchangeable; [registration arms](registration_arms.html) is the one the
manuscript needs.

- [Run QC — the study samples](registration_run_qc.html) — the registration QC of the
  run that produced the analysed data: VALIS's or STARE's own registration error
  (including STARE's per-tile spatial map) and the independent DAPI-nucleus overlap
  cross-check. Reads `data/mirage/` and needs nothing else — the only page that
  renders from a pipeline run alone, with no counts, no clinical table and no gating.
- [Registration arms](registration_arms.html) — the study slides registered **once
  per configuration** (`memory_mode` high/low crossed with `reg_micro_reg` 0/1/2 =
  six arms). Ranks the arms on real tissue and separates what each knob buys. Also
  where the comparability rules live: mirage's `rigid` QC stage means affine ∘
  micro-rigid at depth ≥ 1, so it cannot be compared across depths.

## Part 4 — Benchmarks

Both read mirage's `benchmarks/` **sweep**, which runs on synthetic images with a
known injected transform to measure cost and scaling. They say nothing about your
samples — part 3 does that.

- [Registration accuracy — synthetic sweep](benchmark_registration.html) — VALIS
  feature rTRE per stage, the segmentation-overlap cross-check, accuracy vs cost, and
  an agreement view of the two estimates.
- [Pipeline benchmarks TODO](benchmark_pipeline.html) — resource scaling, I/O volume,
  whole-pipeline cost and segmentation-method comparison.

## Marker QC (internal, no external reference)

- [Marker QC](marker_qc.html) — whether the FlowPath gating is
  self-consistent before anything is compared against it: per-channel usability and
  bimodality, phenotype ↔ marker agreement, morphology by phenotype, then lineage
  leakage (CD45 firing inside tumour phenotypes, PANCK inside immune ones) and
  marker-pair exclusivity. Replaces the former `ihc_qc` and `exclusivity` pages,
  which asked the same question of the same table from two directions.
